brief.subject: Ghana's timber licence and a $650M coffee deal
brief.headline: Ghana's EU Timber Licence After 16 Years; Kraft Heinz Sells North American Coffee Unit
brief.dek: Ghana's EU timber partnership produces a new sustainable timber licence, and Kraft Heinz agrees a $650 million coffee divestment.
brief.lede: Ghana now has a licence to sell sustainable timber after a 16-year partnership process with the EU. No new EUDR deadline or guidance news surfaced today.

sections.heading: Ghana gets EU timber licence
bullets: Ghana now has a licence to sell sustainable timber, a key credential for wood exporters targeting EU buyers.
The licence follows a 16-year Voluntary Partnership Agreement (VPA) process with the European Union.
Europe is a major market for Ghanaian timber, so legality credentials directly affect market access.
The VPA also aimed to strengthen national forest governance, which shapes how exporters document legal sourcing.

sections.heading: Kraft Heinz exits North American coffee
bullets: Kraft Heinz will sell its North American coffee business to One Rock for $650 million.
Kraft Heinz keeps a 30% stake, so coffee suppliers face a partial change in buyer ownership.
Kraft Heinz plans to use the cash proceeds to cut debt.

items.title: Kraft Heinz to sell North American coffee business for $650M
items.snippet: Kraft Heinz will sell its North American coffee business to One Rock for $650 million, retain a 30% stake and use cash proceeds to reduce debt.
